earnings.title: November 5, 2026
highlights: Third-quarter revenues of $9.4 billion; GAAP 1 Net Income of $1,140 million, or 12.1% of sales
EBITDA 2 in the third quarter was a record 18.9% of sales; Diluted EPS of $8.25
Net income attributable to Cummins in the third quarter was $1.14 billion, or $8.25 per diluted share, compared with $536 million, or $3.86 per diluted share, in 2025.
The company returned $661 million to shareholders in the third quarter in the form of cash dividends and share repurchases
Third-quarter 2026 revenues of $9.4 billion increased 13% from the same quarter in 2025.

quotes.text: We delivered record EBITDA and earnings per share in the third quarter, led by continued strength in our Power Systems business.
quotes.by: Jennifer Rumsey, Chair and CEO of Cummins

quotes.text: We have updated our full-year revenue and profitability guidance primarily due to continued weaker than expected pickup truck demand in North America, which impacted our third quarter and is expected to persist through the end of this year.

outlook: The company expects full-year revenue growth of approximately 10% and EBITDA of approximately 18.2%
Based on its current forecast, Cummins expects revenue growth of approximately 10% compared to our prior guidance of 10% to 13%.

EBITDA margins are expected to be approximately 18.2%, consistent with our prior guidance range of 18% to 18.5%, and excluding charges related to the sale of the low-pressure fuel cell business in the first quarter.

items.heading: Evolving environmental and climate change legislation and regulatory initiatives may adversely impact our operations, could impact the competitive landscape within our markets and could negatively affect demand for our products.
We operate our business on a global basis and changes in tariffs and other trade disruptions could adversely impact the demand for our products and our competitive position.

We operate our business on a global basis and changes in international, national and regional trade laws, regulations and policies affecting and/or restricting international trade could adversely impact the demand for our products and our competitive position.
Deregulation could impair our investments in future products and negatively impact our long-term growth and competitiveness.
Unanticipated changes in our effective tax rate, the adoption of new tax legislation or exposure to additional income tax liabilities could adversely affect our profitability.
Our global operations are subject to laws and regulations that impose significant compliance costs and create reputational and legal risk.
